content.text: {"headline":"Recommend no action (P0): predicted service level is 100% on both queues for 15:00-17:00, at no extra cost.","why":"General calls have run 20-41% above forecast since 14:00 (498 vs 414 forecast from 13:00 to 15:00), and service level dropped to 32.4% at 14:15. Even so, the model predicts 100% service level for both payments and general over the 15:00-17:00 window with no changes. It also predicts 0% abandons and 96.9% for the rest of the day, above the 80% target. The cause of the surge is unknown. The extra calls are spread across normal reasons, and the morning login outage (INC-20261024-1535) does not explain the afternoon rise. Every option that acts only adds cover at 19:00-20:00, outside the disruption window, so none of them changes the window forecast.","trade_offs":["P3 (overtime for 5 general agents 19:00-20:00, INR 360, no policy issues) lifts the rest-of-day figure only from 96.9% to 97.4%. It is a reasonable fallback if the surge carries into the evening.","P1, P2 and P4 break policy MOV-01: no cross-skilled payments agents are on shift at 19:00, so those moves cannot happen.","P4 (INR 540) gives the best rest-of-day figure, 97.7%, but it depends on the same impossible payments-to-general move."],"watch":"The surge on general is unexplained. Check intervals after 15:00 to see whether volume keeps running above forecast, and be ready to approve P3 overtime if it does. Separately, ask the floor why payments had only 21-23 agents on phones against 27 planned at 14:30-14:45 when just 1 absence is logged; possible reasons include breaks, meetings or login problems."}
